subject: Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model

messages.author: 13b95c7a86073d8e
messages.subject: Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Dear all,

I am learning INLA's spde models and am trying to figure out how to use the extraconstr augment to specify "orthogonal" constraints to correct for spatial confounding (between location-specific covariates and spatial random effects).  I have run the code (in the file "example_covariate_shrinkage_spde.R") Daniel posted on June 22, 2015.  I hope Daniel or others on the list can help me with the following two general questions.
Is there an example, which specifies extraconstr in a space-time spde model with a random term like f(field.i, model=spede, group=group.id, control.group=list(model='ar1')?  Do I need to worry about any dimension mismatch between the QR factorized covariate matrix and spde because of the ar1 model in the spde term?
Also, does INLA have other specific spatial models, based on the spde and bym,  for spatial confounding?  Many thanks in advance.

Best,

Guiming

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Hi,

First, please note that while one would _like_ these constraints to
"correct for" spatial confounding, in practice they don't necessarily
do that. They can sometimes _help_, but you still need to be careful
about over-interpreting estimated coefficients.

That said, the extraconstr constraints in inla.spde.(pc)matern operate
on the spatial domain only, which when combined with a "group" model
such as ar1 means that it applies to each time point individually,
which is very different to applying it to the temporal average field,
for example.

Only the "iid" replication model has a workaround for this, by
constructing the replication and any associated constraints in
inla.spde2.matern itself (using n.iid.group, and not using "group" in
f() at all), which allows more general constraints on the full model.

A possibly better and more general alternative is to _not_ impose
constraints in the model, but instead choose more carefully how to
interpret the output, by computing appropriate contrasts. (A bit messy
in R-INLA itself; a bit easier in our http://inlabru.org/ package
(still in development but most things related to this already works))

Finn

parts:
Hi Finn and Havard,

Thanks for your replies and suggestions.  Finn suggests that one can carefully interpret the model outputs instead of using constraints.  Can I use correlation between location-specific observations and estimated spatial random effects (e.g., retrieved with A%*%mod$summary.rand$field.index$mean) at the same locations to indicate how an observed variable may influence response variables via a spatial process?  

In a case, model selection using DIC led to a model excluding a covariate as an main effect; however, the covariate was correlated with spatial random effects (estimated by f(..,model=spde)).  Non-parametric correlation (Mantel-test like) indicated cross correlation between response variable and covariate within a distance of ca. 200 km. If I can interpret the SPDE results use the correlation, I would suggest that the covariate may influence the response variable through a spatial process.  Thanks again.

Best,

Guiming

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Hi,

I meant that one _must_ be careful; I did not mean that there is
always and necessarily a good way of doing it.

What you describe can give indications of influence, yes, but due to
posterior correlations it's not always clear.
In the case of a spatial covariate that is reasonably smooth, it will
be confounded with a spatial field term.
Ideally, one would then like the linear covariate effect to capture
all linear effect, and the field only be substantially
non-zero if required, but that requires the parameter priors for the
field component to be chosen appropriately.
Make sure to use inla.spde2.pcmatern, since the PC-prior was developed
to help with this.

I don't understand the last part of your question in a Bayesian
hierarchical model framework,
with a sum of a linear covariate effect and a random field component.
You seem to be talking about
a physical process through which the covariate has an effect.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Hi Finn,

Your suggestions help!  I went through the examples of inla.spde2.pcmatern and coded the constraint as you suggested.  Could you take a look at the following segment code to see if I handled f(field, model=spde) correctly?  I followed your suggestion of not using group at all in the f(), so I guess, then, I should not use model="ar1" either.  Thanks in advance!

Guiming

n.data=27*12  #27 sites and 12 years
X = cbind(Intercept=rep(1,n.data),temp=maxtemp, lal=lats)  #lat-latitudes of sites
Q = qr.Q(qr(X))
n.covariates=3

A.est = inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
       loc = as.matrix(obsloc))  #obsloc - latitudes and longitudes with necessary repeats

field.indices =
       inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=mesh$n)

spde = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh=mesh, constr=T,
       n.iid.group = yrs,           #yrs =12
       prior.range=c(0.01,0.1), prior.sigma=c(100,0.1),
       extraconstr = list(A = as.matrix(t(Q)%*%A.est), e= rep(0, n.covariates))
)

stack.est1 = inla.stack(data=list(y=l2,e=ll),                 #e-offset
       A=list(A.est, 1),
       effects= list(c(field.indices,list(Intercept=1)),
             list(temp=maxtemp, lat=lats,pop=pop, pop2=pop2)),
       tag="est")

f4 <- (y ~ -1 + Intercept + temp+ lat+f(pop,model="iid")+  #pop -site index
      f(pop2, temp, model="iid") +
      f(field, model=spde))

mod4b = inla(f4,
       data=inla.stack.data(stack.est1, spde=spde),
       family="nbinomial",E=e,
       control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est1), compute=FALSE),
       control.compute=list(cpo=T, dic=T),
       control.inla = list(reordering = "metis")

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Your code, if it runs without error (which I don't think it will),
seems to construct a constraint for each timepoint, but then averages
that constraint over all timepoints. I suspect that what you're after
is rather a constraint against the observation locations in
space-time.
(If you want an AR model in time, this method doesn't work, so I'll
assume that you're happy with a temporal iid model)

You need to change the order of the code, and modify/add some parameters:

A.est = inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
loc = as.matrix(obsloc), group=obsyear, n.group=yrs)

spde = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh=mesh, constr=T,
n.iid.group = yrs, #yrs =12
prior.range=c(0.01,0.1), prior.sigma=c(100,0.1),
extraconstr = list(A = as.matrix(t(Q)%*%A.est), e= rep(0, n.covariates))
)

field.indices =
inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=spde$n.spde)

(You should always use spde$n.spde in inla.spde.make.index. It doesn't
usually matter, but in this case it's essential, since
n.spde will be mesh$n * yrs)

Finn

>> > use correlation between location-specific observations and estimated
>> > spatial
>> > random effects (e.g., retrieved with
>> > A%*%mod$summary.rand$field.index$mean)
>> > at the same locations to indicate how an observed variable may influence
>> > response variables via a spatial process?
>> >
>> > In a case, model selection using DIC led to a model excluding a
>> > covariate as
>> > an main effect; however, the covariate was correlated with spatial
>> > random
>> > effects (estimated by f(..,model=spde)). Non-parametric correlation
>> > (Mantel-test like) indicated cross correlation between response variable
>> > and
>> > covariate within a distance of ca. 200 km. If I can interpret the SPDE
>> > results use the correlation, I would suggest that the covariate may
>> > influence the response variable through a spatial process. Thanks
>> > again.
>> >
>> > Best,
>> >
>> > Guiming
>> >
>> > On Tuesday, July 18, 2017 at 8:54:56 AM UTC-5, Finn Lindgren wrote:
>> >>
>> >> Hi,
>> >>
>> >> First, please note that while one would _like_ these constraints to
>> >> "correct for" spatial confounding, in practice they don't necessarily
>> >> do that. They can sometimes _help_, but you still need to be careful
>> >> about over-interpreting estimated coefficients.
>> >>
>> >> That said, the extraconstr constraints in inla.spde.(pc)matern operate
>> >> on the spatial domain only, which when combined with a "group" model
>> >> such as ar1 means that it applies to each time point individually,
>> >> which is very different to applying it to the temporal average field,
>> >> for example.
>> >>
>> >> Only the "iid" replication model has a workaround for this, by
>> >> constructing the replication and any associated constraints in
>> >> inla.spde2.matern itself (using n.iid.group, and not using "group" in
>> >> f() at all), which allows more general constraints on the full model.
>> >>
>> >> A possibly better and more general alternative is to _not_ impose
>> >> constraints in the model, but instead choose more carefully how to
>> >> interpret the output, by computing appropriate contrasts. (A bit messy
>> >> in R-INLA itself; a bit easier in our http://inlabru.org/ package
>> >> (still in development but most things related to this already works))
>> >>
>> >> Finn

messages.subject: Re: Specification of extraconstr for a spde space-time model
parts:
Hi Finn,

Greatly appreciate your input and suggestions!!

I have a question about your last comment.  Should I use: field.indices =
  inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=mesh$n*yrs) or field.indices =
  inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=mesh$n)?  You mentioned n.spde should be mesh$n*yrs in this case.

I noticed that if I used the ar1 for group and set constr=T in spde, 95$ CI excluded zero, contrary to my original model with the default constr setting.  Is the difference related to the model identifiability issue?  I am trying to figure out any guideline for choosing constr setting.

My previous code ran OK, but not it seems to me the code may be incorrect because of incorrect dimensions of indices and A matrix.

Best regards,

Guiming

On Tuesday, July 18, 2017 at 8:38:44 AM UTC-5, Guiming Wang wrote:
Dear all,

I am learning INLA's spde models and am trying to figure out how to use the extraconstr augment to specify "orthogonal" constraints to correct for spatial confounding (between location-specific covariates and spatial random effects).  I have run the code (in the file "example_covariate_shrinkage_spde.R") Daniel posted on June 22, 2015.  I hope Daniel or others on the list can help me with the following two general questions.
Is there an example, which specifies extraconstr in a space-time spde model with a random term like f(field.i, model=spede, group=group.id, control.group=list(model='ar1')?  Do I need to worry about any dimension mismatch between the QR factorized covariate matrix and spde because of the ar1 model in the spde term?
Also, does INLA have other specific spatial models, based on the spde and bym,  for spatial confounding?  Many thanks in advance.

Best,

Guiming
